mainTopic: Daytime and nighttime מצוות; the new chapter on how the מגילה and the תורה are read, and standing for תורה.
overview: This amud finishes the chapter הקורא למפרע and opens a new one. First, the גמרא gives sources for the משנה's daytime מצוות (סוטה, עגלה ערופה, טהרת מצורע) and its nighttime מצוות (קצירת העומר, הקטר חלבים ואברים). It then asks what each זה הכלל adds. The daytime rule adds סידור בזיכין and סילוק בזיכין, which follows רבי יוסי. The nighttime rule adds eating the פסח all night, which goes against רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. After the הדרן, a new משנה teaches that the מגילה may be read standing or sitting, by one reader or two. It also sets how many people are called to the תורה on each kind of day. The גמרא learns from 'ואתה פה עמד עמדי' that the תורה must be read standing, and it tells how learning moved from standing to sitting after רבן גמליאל died. It gives four answers to whether משה sat or stood on the mountain. Finally, it returns to the משנה's line about two people reading the מגילה together, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the source: the סוטה drinks only by day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes its comparison between the סוטה procedure and a court judgment. A judgment happens by day, so the סוטה drinks by day too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as a court judgment is done by day, so too here the סוטה is done by day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof that began on the previous amud. It concludes that the סוטה is given the bitter water only during the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the previous amud, the גמרא linked the word 'תורה' in the סוטה passage to the word 'משפט' (judgment) in another verse. A court judgment may only be done by day. Because of that link, the סוטה procedure takes on the same daytime rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A court judgment, which may only be done by day
'So too here': applying the rule from one case to the other
A woman suspected of adultery who drinks the bitter water

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the END of a proof that started on the previous amud. It is not a brand-new idea, so don't look for the beginning of the argument here.

phrases.english: Just as judgment is by day
phrases.notes: A court may only rule by day

phrases.english: so too here, by day.
phrases.notes: The סוטה drinks only in the daytime

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה מִשְׁפָּט בַּיּוֹם אַף כָּאן בַּיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the סוטה derivation begun on the previous amud
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The סוטה drinking is a daytime procedure, learned from the comparison to משפט.

steps.title: Why breaking the heifer's neck is done by day
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ינאי explains that the עגלה ערופה is done by day. The Torah calls it a כפרה, so it is treated like קדשים, which are done by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for breaking the heifer's neck: the school of רבי ינאי said that the Torah uses the word 'atonement' for it, just like it does for קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for the משנה's rule that עגלה ערופה must be done by day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says 'כפר לעמך ישראל' about the heifer. The word כפרה connects it to קדשים, and all Temple service with קדשים must be done by day. So the heifer takes on that same daytime rule, even though it is not brought in the Temple.

keyTerms.meaning: Breaking the neck of the heifer, done when a murdered body is found and the killer is unknown
The school (students) of רבי ינאי
Atonement
Sacred offerings, which are brought only by day

phrases.english: And for breaking the neck of the heifer,
phrases.notes: The next item in the משנה's daytime list

phrases.english: the school of Rabbi Yannai said:
atonement is written about it, like sacred offerings.
phrases.notes: So it follows the daytime rule of קדשים

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלַעֲרִיפַת הָעֶגְלָה אָמְרִי דְּבֵי רַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next item on the משנה's daytime list
steps.raayaObject: The משנה's ruling that עגלה ערופה is done by day
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word כפרה in the heifer passage, which compares it to קדשים

steps.title: Why the leper's purification is done by day
steps.stepSummary: The verse says 'on the day of his purification', which teaches that טהרת מצורע is done by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for purifying the מצורע, as it is written: 'This shall be the law of the מצורע on the day of his purification.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a verse as the source for the daytime rule of טהרת מצורע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the source is simple and direct. The word 'ביום' (on the day) is right in the verse, so no comparison to another case is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The purification process of a person afflicted with צרעת
'As it is written': introduces a verse
On the day, meaning in the daytime

phrases.english: And for purifying the leper, as it is written:
"This shall be the law of the leper
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:2

phrases.english: on the day of his cleansing."
phrases.notes: 'On the day' is the source for daytime

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues giving sources for the daytime list
steps.raayaObject: The משנה's ruling that טהרת מצורע is done by day
steps.whatToRemember: Each daytime מצוה in the משנה has a source. Some come from comparisons (סוטה, עגלה ערופה), and some come straight from the word 'ביום' (מצורע).

steps.title: Why reaping the עומר is done at night
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now turns to the משנה's nighttime list. It cites a known teaching: reaping and counting the עומר are done at night, but bringing the offering is done by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The whole night is valid for reaping the עומר', as the Master said: reaping and counting are at night, and bringing is by day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the start of the משנה's nighttime list. It then supports the rule with a teaching from elsewhere (מסכת מנחות).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every part of the עומר מצוה has the same time. Reaping and counting belong to the night, while the actual offering in the Temple belongs to the day. The משנה lists only the reaping because that is the nighttime part.

keyTerms.meaning: Reaping the barley for the עומר offering
Counting (of the עומר)
Bringing the offering to the Temple

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the whole עומר מצוה is at night. Only reaping and counting are at night. Bringing the offering is by day.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַלַּיְלָה כָּשֵׁר לִקְצִירַת הָעוֹמֶר וְכוּ׳,
phrases.english: The entire night is valid for reaping the omer, etc.
phrases.notes: Quote of the משנה

phrases.english: as the Master said:
reaping and counting are at night,
and bringing is by day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the daytime list to the nighttime list
steps.raayaObject: The משנה's ruling that reaping the עומר is valid all night
steps.raayaSupportSource: A teaching of 'מר' found in מסכת מנחות

steps.title: Why burning fats and limbs may be done all night
steps.stepSummary: The verse 'all night until the morning' shows that the fats and limbs may be burned on the altar through the whole night.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for burning the fats and limbs, as it is written: 'all night until the morning.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a verse as the source for burning offering parts on the altar at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about the עולה says it burns on the altar 'all night until the morning'. This shows that the whole night is valid for burning the fats and limbs.

keyTerms.meaning: Burning the fats and limbs of offerings on the altar
Until the morning

phrases.english: And for burning fats and limbs, as it is written:
"all night until the morning."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:2

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the nighttime list with the next item
steps.raayaObject: The משנה's ruling that הקטר חלבים ואברים is valid all night
steps.whatToRemember: Nighttime מצוות also have sources: the עומר from a known teaching, and burning on the altar from 'כל הלילה עד הבוקר'.

steps.title: What does the general rule add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's closing rule, 'זה הכלל'. It then asks what that rule includes, since the משנה already listed its examples.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'This is the rule: something whose מצוה is by day is valid the whole day.' What does 'this is the rule' come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's general rule and asks what extra case it covers. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes that a 'זה הכלל' after a list must be adding something that is not on the list. Otherwise the rule would be extra words. So it searches for a daytime מצוה that the משנה did not name.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is the rule': a general principle that closes a list
'To include what?': asking what extra case is added
Whose מצוה is in the daytime

phrases.english: This is the principle:
phrases.notes: Quote of the משנה

phrases.english: something whose מצוה is by day
is valid the entire day.
"This is the principle" is to include what?
phrases.notes: The question of the גמרא

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the lists, the גמרא turns to the משנה's closing principle
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case, not listed in the משנה, is included by 'זה הכלל'

steps.title: It includes arranging and removing the frankincense bowls
steps.stepSummary: The rule includes setting the frankincense bowls next to the לחם הפנים and removing them. The Torah gives no time for these, so the rule tells us they are valid all day.
steps.simpleTranslation: To include the arranging of the frankincense bowls and the removing of the frankincense bowls.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. 'זה הכלל' comes to include סידור בזיכין and סילוק בזיכין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bowls of frankincense sat beside the לחם הפנים on the שולחן. They were placed there on שבת and taken away the next שבת. Since no verse gives a specific time for this, the general rule teaches that it may be done any time during the day.

keyTerms.meaning: Arranging the frankincense bowls beside the לחם הפנים
Removing the frankincense bowls at the end of the week
The showbread on the Temple table

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the גמרא reads a 'זה הכלל': the general rule is not extra words, but quietly adds cases the list left out.

phrases.english: To include the arranging of the frankincense bowls
and the removal of the bowls,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues into the next passage

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: זה הכלל includes סידור בזיכין and סילוק בזיכין, which have no time stated in the verse.

steps.title: This fits רבי יוסי, who allows a gap in the bread changeover
steps.stepSummary: The answer from step 7 follows רבי יוסי, who says the old לחם הפנים can be removed in the morning and the new set out in the evening.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this follows רבי יוסי. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יוסי says, if someone removed the old bread in the morning and set out the new bread in the evening, nothing is wrong with that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows which opinion its answer from step 7 depends on. It brings a ברייתא where רבי יוסי allows a gap of time between removing the old bread and placing the new bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'it is valid all day' only works if the changeover can be spread across the day. רבי יוסי says it can, so the משנה must follow him. The other חכמים say the new bread must be placed right away, so for them there is no 'all day' span.

keyTerms.meaning: He removed
He arranged, set out
There is nothing wrong with that

phrases.english: And it is like Rabbi Yosei.
phrases.notes: The answer from step 7 fits his opinion.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Yosei says:
If he removed the old bread in the morning,
and set out the new bread toward evening,
there is nothing wrong with this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the תנא whose view the answer in step 7 requires.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה's 'all day' rule for the frankincense bowls follows רבי יוסי

steps.title: How רבי יוסי reads 'always before ה׳'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי explains that 'תמיד' only means the table should never go a whole day without bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do I fulfill the verse 'before ה׳ always'? It means that the table should not be without bread.
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the same ברייתא, רבי יוסי answers an obvious objection to his view. The verse says the bread must be there 'always', so how can there be a gap?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plain reading of 'תמיד' suggests the bread must be on the table every moment. רבי יוסי reads it more loosely: as long as the table has bread at some point each day, that counts as 'always'. This lets him allow the morning-to-evening gap.

keyTerms.meaning: And how do I fulfill (this verse)?
Always, continually
The table in the משכן/מקדש that held the לחם הפנים

phrases.english: And how do I uphold
"before the Lord continually"?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 24:8, said about the לחם הפנים.

phrases.english: That the table should not be without bread.
phrases.notes: That is, not for an entire day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבי יוסי's ruling from step 8 against the verse 'תמיד'.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'תמיד' means the bread must be on the table every moment, so no gap is allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'תמיד' only means the table should never go a full day without bread.

steps.title: What does the nighttime general rule add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that a nighttime מצוה is valid all night and asks what it adds.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Something whose מצוה is at night is valid the whole night.' What does this come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second half of the משנה's 'זה הכלל', the nighttime rule. It asks what extra case this rule covers. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already listed nighttime examples, like reaping the עומר and burning fats and limbs. A general rule should add something new, so the גמרא asks what that is. This matches the question it asked about the daytime rule in step 6.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose מצוה is at night
To include what?

phrases.english: Something whose מצוה is at night
is valid the entire night.
What does this come to include?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 6: the same question, now about the nighttime rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case, not already listed, the nighttime general rule adds

steps.title: It adds eating the קרבן פסח all night
steps.stepSummary: The rule adds that the קרבן פסח may be eaten all night, so the משנה does not follow רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include eating the פסח offerings, and this is not like רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the rule teaches the קרבן פסח may be eaten the whole night. It also points out that this disagrees with רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating the פסח is a nighttime מצוה, so the rule makes it valid until dawn. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה holds it may only be eaten until midnight. So the משנה must follow the opposing view.

keyTerms.meaning: Eating of the קרבן פסח
And not in accordance with

phrases.english: To include the eating of Paschal offerings,
and not in accordance with Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The nighttime rule includes eating the קרבן פסח all night, against רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's source: until midnight
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה learns from the words 'this night' that the פסח may be eaten only until midnight.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'And they shall eat the meat on this night.' רבי אלעזר בן עזריה said: it says here 'on this night', and it says later 'And I will pass through the land of Egypt on this night'. Just as there it was until midnight, so too here it is until midnight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's opinion, which the משנה rejects. He links two verses that both say 'בלילה הזה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a גזירה שווה: the same words in two places teach that the two share a rule. ה׳ passed through מצרים at midnight, so the 'night' of eating the פסח also ends at midnight. The משנה's 'all night' rule disagrees with this.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning a law from identical words in two verses
It is said here
And it is said further on
Until midnight

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's two general rules add new cases. The daytime rule adds the frankincense bowls all day, which follows רבי יוסי. The nighttime rule adds eating the פסח all night, which is against רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'וּדְלָא כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה' means the משנה disagrees with him. The ברייתא here is brought to show his view, not to support the משנה.

phrases.english: As it is taught:
"And they shall eat the meat on this night"
phrases.notes: שמות 12:8

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya said:
It is stated here, "on this night",
and it is stated further on:
"And I will pass through the land of Egypt on this night"
phrases.notes: שמות 12:12

phrases.english: Just as there it was until midnight,
so too here, until midnight.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: וְאָכְלוּ אֶת הַבָּשָׂר בַּלַּיְלָה הַזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the ברייתא behind the opinion that step 11 says the משנה rejects.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אלעזר בן עזריה limits eating the פסח to midnight
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא with a גזירה שווה from 'בלילה הזה' (שמות 12:8 and 12:12)

steps.title: הדרן — Closing the chapter הקורא למפרע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא formally closes the chapter called הקורא למפרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter 'One who reads out of order.'
steps.whatsHappening: The chapter about reading the מגילה out of order is now finished. This line is a goodbye to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הדרן is not part of any argument. It is a traditional closing line that marks the end of a chapter and expresses the hope to come back and learn it again. The topic of the previous chapter (and its last discussion, about the פסח and nighttime מצוות) is now done.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. This is the closing formula at the end of a chapter.
Out of order, backwards. This is the name of the chapter being closed.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not try to connect this line to the argument about רבי אלעזר בן עזריה and the פסח. That discussion is over. This line just ends the chapter.

phrases.english: We will return to you
'One who reads out of order'
phrases.notes: The chapter's name, taken from its opening words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter whose final discussion appeared in steps 10–12.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter הקורא למפרע is complete. A new chapter begins next.

steps.title: New chapter: rules for reading the מגילה
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה teaches that the מגילה may be read standing or sitting, by one or two readers, and that the ברכה depends on local custom.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who reads the מגילה may stand or sit. If one person read it, or two people read it, they have fulfilled their obligation. In a place where people are used to saying a ברכה, he should say it. In a place where they are not, he should not say it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter opens with a משנה. It gives three simple rules about how the מגילה is read.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rule 1: the reader's position does not matter, so standing or sitting is fine. Rule 2: even if two people read together at the same time, the listeners still fulfill the מצוה. Rule 3: whether to say a ברכה over the reading follows the custom of each place.

keyTerms.meaning: Standing or sitting. Either is allowed.
They have fulfilled their obligation.
A place where it is the custom.
To say a ברכה.

steps.confusionAlert: 'Read it, two' does not mean two people taking turns. It means two people reading the מגילה at the same time, together. Even so, the listeners are יוצא.

phrases.english: One who reads the Megillah
may stand or sit.
Whether one read it, or two read it together
they have fulfilled the obligation.
In a place where they are accustomed to bless, he should bless,
and where they are accustomed not to bless, he should not bless.
phrases.notes: The גמרא later explains that this refers to the ברכה said after the reading.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new chapter right after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מגילה may be read standing or sitting, by one reader or two reading together, and the ברכה follows local custom.

steps.title: Three readers on Monday, Thursday, and שבת מנחה
steps.stepSummary: On Monday and Thursday mornings and at שבת מנחה, exactly three people read from the תורה. There is no הפטרה, and only the first and last readers say ברכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: On Monday, Thursday, and at מנחה on שבת, three people read. We do not call fewer than three or more than three, and we do not finish with a reading from the נביאים. The one who opens the תורה reading says a ברכה before it, and the one who closes it says a ברכה after it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves on from the מגילה to public תורה reading. It starts with the days when three people are called up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The number three is fixed: no fewer and no more. These short readings have no הפטרה. In the time of the משנה, only the first reader said the ברכה before the reading, and only the last reader said the ברכה after it. The middle reader said none.

keyTerms.meaning: On Monday and Thursday.
We do not call fewer.
We do not call more.
Concluding with a reading from the נביאים (the הפטרה).
The one who opens and the one who closes the reading.

steps.confusionAlert: Today every עולה says a ברכה both before and after. The גמרא later explains that this was changed by תקנה. The משנה describes the original practice.

phrases.english: On Monday, Thursday, and on Shabbat at Minchah
three people read.
We do not reduce from them,
and we do not add to them,
and we do not conclude with the Prophets.
The one who opens and the one who closes the Torah reading
bless before it and after it.
phrases.notes: The opener blesses before, and the closer blesses after.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּשֵׁנִי וַחֲמִישִׁי בַּשַּׁבָּת בַּמִּנְחָה קוֹרִין שְׁלֹשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה, moving from מגילה reading to תורה reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On Monday, Thursday, and שבת מנחה, exactly three people read, there is no הפטרה, and only the first and last readers say ברכות.

steps.title: Four readers on ראש חודש and חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: On ראש חודש and חול המועד, exactly four people read from the תורה. The other rules are the same: no הפטרה, and ברכות only by the first and last readers.
steps.simpleTranslation: On ראש חודש and on חול המועד, four people read. We do not call fewer than four or more than four, and we do not finish with a reading from the נביאים. The one who opens the תורה reading says a ברכה before it, and the one who closes it says a ברכה after it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה goes up one level to days with more holiness and adds a fourth reader. The rest of the rules repeat word for word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only change from the previous step is the number: four instead of three. This shows a pattern. Days with more significance get more people called to the תורה. The rules about no adding, no subtracting, no הפטרה, and ברכות only at the start and end stay exactly the same.

keyTerms.meaning: Days of the New Moon (ראש חודש).
The intermediate days of a Festival (חול המועד).
Four.

steps.whatToRemember: Count the readers by the importance of the day: three on Monday, Thursday, and שבת מנחה, and four on ראש חודש and חול המועד. On these days there is no adding, no subtracting, and no הפטרה. Originally, only the first and last readers said ברכות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a ladder of readers that the משנה continues afterward for יום טוב, יום כיפור, and שבת. The גמרא will look for the reason behind each number.

phrases.english: On New Moons and on the intermediate days of a Festival
four people read.
We do not reduce from them,
and we do not add to them,
and we do not conclude with the Prophets.
The one who opens and the one who closes the Torah reading
bless before it and after it.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּרָאשֵׁי חֳדָשִׁים וּבְחוּלּוֹ שֶׁל מוֹעֵד קוֹרִין אַרְבָּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same structure as step 15, with the number of readers raised to four for days of greater significance.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On ראש חודש and חול המועד, exactly four people read, there is no הפטרה, and only the first and last readers say ברכות.

steps.title: The general rule for the number of readers
steps.stepSummary: Days with a מוסף that are not יום טוב get four readers. יום טוב gets five, יום הכפורים six, and שבת seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the rule: any day that has a מוסף but is not יום טוב, four people read. On יום טוב, five. On יום הכפורים, six. On שבת, seven.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives one simple rule that ranks the special days by how many people are called up to the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The more important the day, the more readers it gets. ראש חודש and חול המועד (from step 16) are the 'מוסף but not יום טוב' days and get four. Then the count goes up one by one: יום טוב, then יום הכפורים, then שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the general rule
The extra קרבן brought on special days
A Festival day
The Day of Atonement

steps.whatToRemember: Count by importance: 3 for weekdays and שבת מנחה, 4 for ראש חודש and חול המועד, 5 for יום טוב, 6 for יום הכפורים, 7 for שבת.

phrases.english: This is the general rule:
any day that has an additional offering
phrases.notes: Meaning ראש חודש and חול המועד

phrases.english: and is not a Festival, four people read;
on a Festival, five;
on Yom Kippur, six;
on Shabbat, seven.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה הַכְּלָל: כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ מוּסָף וְאֵינוֹ יוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the list from steps 15-16 into one general rule and carries it up to שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Number of readers: מוסף days that are not יום טוב get 4, יום טוב 5, יום הכפורים 6, שבת 7.

steps.title: Adding readers, the הפטרה, and the ברכות
steps.stepSummary: You may add readers but not subtract. These days end with a reading from the נביאים, and only the first and last readers say a ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You may not have fewer readers, but you may add more. A reading from the Prophets is added at the end. The one who opens the תורה reading says a ברכה before it, and the one who closes says a ברכה after it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives three extra rules for the days it just listed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The number of readers is a minimum, not a maximum, so you may add but never go below it. These days have a הפטרה, unlike the weekday readings in step 15. The ברכות work the same as before: only the opener and the closer make them.

keyTerms.meaning: One may not decrease
One may add
They conclude with a reading from the Prophets
The one who opens and the one who closes

steps.confusionAlert: In the time of the משנה, only the first reader said a ברכה before and only the last said one after. Today every person called up says both ברכות. That is a later practice, not what this משנה describes.

phrases.english: One may not decrease from them,
but one may add to them,
and one concludes with the Prophets.
The one who opens and the one who closes in the Torah
recite a blessing before it and after it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מֵהֶן, אֲבָל מוֹסִיפִין עֲלֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds rules that apply to the days listed in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The number is a minimum. A הפטרה is read. Only the first and last readers make ברכות.
steps.whatToRemember: On these special days, the number of readers is a minimum and a הפטרה is read.

steps.title: The תורה is not like the מגילה: it must be read standing
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that sitting is allowed for the מגילה but not for reading the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: which is not so for the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts by going back to the משנה's first rule, that the מגילה may be read sitting, and quotes a ברייתא saying the תורה is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in step 14 allowed the מגילה to be read sitting. The ברייתא adds that this leniency does not apply to the תורה, which must be read standing. This sets up the question of where that rule comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: Which is not the case
The discussion that explains the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was taught:
which is not so for the Torah.
phrases.notes: The Torah reading must be done standing

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה's ruling in step 14 that the מגילה may be read sitting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תורה must be read standing.

steps.title: Asking for the source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that the תורה must be read standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where are these matters learned?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the ברייתא's rule. This sets up the next step, where רבי אבהו gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a real request for a source, not an attack on the rule. The גמרא wants to find the פסוק behind the requirement to stand.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these things learned?

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק teaches that the תורה must be read standing.

steps.title: רבי אבהו's source: 'Stand here with Me'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו learns the rule from 'ואתה פה עמד עמדי'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: because the פסוק says, 'And you, stand here with Me.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the question with a פסוק about how משה received the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳ told משה to stand while receiving the תורה. So whenever the תורה is passed on, as in the public reading, it should be done standing.

keyTerms.meaning: As the verse says
Stand with Me

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
as the verse says:
"But as for you, stand here with Me."
phrases.notes: דברים 5:28

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is 'ואתה פה עמד עמדי': the תורה is received standing.
steps.whatToRemember: We stand for קריאת התורה because משה stood when he received the תורה.

steps.title: As it were, ה׳ Himself was standing
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו reads the word 'עמדי' to mean that, as it were, ה׳ also stood. He says we could not say this if the פסוק did not say it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אבהו said: if the פסוק were not written, it would be impossible to say it. As it were, even ה׳ was standing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו adds a deeper reading of the same פסוק, built on the word 'with Me'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Stand with Me' suggests that ה׳ was standing too. That is such a bold idea that we would only say it because the פסוק itself hints to it. The word 'כביכול' softens it, meaning 'as if it could be said'.

keyTerms.meaning: Were the verse not written
As it were (as if one could say so)
Standing

phrases.english: And Rabbi Abbahu said:
Were the verse not written,
it would be impossible to say it.

phrases.aramaic: כִּבְיָכוֹל אַף הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בַּעֲמִידָה.
phrases.english: As it were, even the Holy One, Blessed be He, was standing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: אִלְמָלֵא מִקְרָא כָּתוּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching by רבי אבהו from the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word 'עמדי' hints that ה׳, as it were, also stood at מתן תורה.

steps.title: A teacher should not sit higher than his student
steps.stepSummary: From the same פסוק, רבי אבהו teaches that a רב should not sit on a couch while his student sits on the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אבהו said: from where do we know that a teacher should not sit on a couch and teach his student who sits on the ground? Because it says, 'And you, stand here with Me.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו gives a third lesson from 'עמד עמדי', this time about how teacher and student should sit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'With Me' shows ה׳ and משה were in the same position. So a teacher and student should also be at the same level, not one high and one low.

keyTerms.meaning: From where (do we know)?
Teacher
On a couch or bed
On the ground

phrases.english: And Rabbi Abbahu said:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן לָרַב שֶׁלֹּא יֵשֵׁב עַל גַּבֵּי מִטָּה
phrases.english: From where is it derived that a teacher should not sit on a couch
and teach his student who sits on the ground?
As it is stated: "But as for you, stand here with Me."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another lesson from the same פסוק, now about teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A teacher and student should be at the same level when learning.

steps.title: תורה was learned standing until רבן גמליאל died
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says תורה was learned only standing from משה until רבן גמליאל. After his death, weakness came to the world and people learned sitting.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: from the days of משה until רבן גמליאל, Torah was learned only standing. When רבן גמליאל died, weakness came to the world, and they learned Torah sitting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with the history of learning Torah standing, which fits the theme of standing for Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Learning was once done standing, like receiving the תורה at סיני. After רבן גמליאל died, people grew physically weaker, so they began learning while sitting.

keyTerms.meaning: Standing
Sitting
Weakness or illness

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
From the days of Moses until Rabban Gamliel,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָיוּ לְמֵדִין תּוֹרָה אֶלָּא מְעוּמָּד.
phrases.english: they would learn Torah only while standing.
When Rabban Gamliel died,
weakness came down to the world,
and they would learn Torah while sitting.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִימוֹת מֹשֶׁה וְעַד רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of standing for Torah with a historical account.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah was learned standing until רבן גמליאל's death. After that, because of weakness, it was learned sitting.

steps.title: Support from a משנה: the honor of תורה ended
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא links the ברייתא to a משנה in סוטה: when רבן גמליאל died, the honor of תורה ended.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what we learned in a משנה: when רבן גמליאל died, the honor of Torah ended.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that a well-known משנה is talking about this same change from standing to sitting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in סוטה says only that 'the honor of Torah ended', without saying how. The ברייתא explains it: standing while learning was a way of honoring the Torah, and that stopped. So the two sources support each other.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what we learned (in a משנה)
The honor of Torah ended

steps.whatToRemember: Standing for Torah is a form of כבוד התורה. That is why we stand for קריאת התורה, and why learning while standing was once the standard.

phrases.english: And this is as we learned in a mishna:
When Rabban Gamliel died,
the honor of Torah ceased.
phrases.notes: משנה in סוטה 49a

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects the ברייתא in step 24 to a משנה that matches it.
steps.raayaObject: The ברייתא's account that the move from standing to sitting began when רבן גמליאל died.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in סוטה 49a: 'משמת רבן גמליאל בטל כבוד תורה'.

steps.title: Two verses disagree: did משה sit or stand on the mountain?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that one פסוק says משה sat on the mountain and another says he stood there.
steps.simpleTranslation: One verse says: 'And I sat on the mountain.' Another verse says: 'And I stood on the mountain.' So which was it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that two פסוקים in ספר דברים seem to contradict each other. This sets up the four answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous steps said Torah was learned standing, based on 'ואתה פה עמד עמדי'. But 'ואשב בהר' says משה sat, which seems to go against that. Both פסוקים describe the same time on the mountain, so the גמרא needs to explain how both can be true.

keyTerms.meaning: One verse says (the opening of a contradiction between two פסוקים)
And I sat on the mountain (דברים ט:ט)
And I stood on the mountain (דברים י:י)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a question against the earlier rule from outside. Both sides are פסוקים about the very same event, and the job is to make them fit together.

phrases.english: One verse says: 'And I sat on the mountain,'
and another verse says: 'And I stood on the mountain'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of learning Torah standing by raising a contradiction between two verses about how משה learned.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two verses that describe משה on the mountain, and with them the idea that Torah was learned standing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One verse says he sat and the other says he stood. Both cannot simply be true at the same moment.

steps.title: רב: stand to learn, sit to review
steps.stepSummary: רב says משה stood while learning new material from ה׳ and sat while reviewing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: He would stand and learn, and sit and review.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the contradiction by splitting the time into two activities. Standing was for learning, and sitting was for reviewing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב, each פסוק describes a different activity. 'עמדתי' refers to receiving the תורה from ה׳, which was done standing out of respect. 'ואשב' refers to משה going over what he learned by himself, which he could do sitting.

keyTerms.meaning: Stands and learns (receives new material)
Sits and reviews (repeats what was learned)

phrases.english: Rav said: he would stand and learn,
and sit and review.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the contradiction in step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Split by activity: each verse describes a different kind of learning.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verses seem to describe one posture for the whole stay.
steps.terutzMaskana: He stood to learn from ה׳ and sat to review on his own.

steps.title: רבי חנינא: neither standing nor sitting, but bowing
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא says משה was bowing, a position between standing and sitting.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: He was not standing and not sitting, but bowing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא gives a second answer. משה was in a bent-over, bowing position, so each פסוק describes part of that posture.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רב, רבי חנינא does not split the time into two parts. He says there was one posture the whole time. Bowing is partly like standing and partly like sitting, so both פסוקים fit it.

keyTerms.meaning: Bowing or bending over

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר: לֹא עוֹמֵד וְלֹא יוֹשֵׁב
phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said: not standing and not sitting,
but rather bowing.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר: לֹא עוֹמֵד וְלֹא יוֹשֵׁב אֶלָּא שׁוֹחֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to the same contradiction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A middle posture that both verses can describe.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Standing and sitting are opposites, so both cannot be true.
steps.terutzMaskana: Bowing is in between, so each verse describes one side of it.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: 'sat' here means 'stayed'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the word 'ישיבה' can mean staying in one place, so 'ואשב' means משה remained on the mountain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The word 'sitting' here only means staying, as it says: 'And you stayed in Kadesh many days.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a third answer. He reads the word 'ואשב' differently, so it no longer describes a sitting position at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן proves from 'ותשבו בקדש ימים רבים' that the word for sitting can mean staying somewhere. So 'ואשב בהר' means 'I stayed on the mountain,' and only 'עמדתי' tells us his posture, which was standing. With this reading, the contradiction disappears completely.

keyTerms.meaning: Sitting, which here can also mean staying or dwelling
A word meaning delay or remaining in a place
And you stayed in קדש many days (דברים א:מו)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: 'sitting' is nothing
but an expression of remaining,
as it is said: 'And you stayed in Kadesh many days.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֵין יְשִׁיבָה אֶלָּא לְשׁוֹן עַכָּבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer. This one changes the meaning of the word instead of describing a posture.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading a word: 'ואשב' means remained, not sat.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ואשב' means staying on the mountain, so משה stood the whole time.

steps.title: רבא: easy material standing, hard material sitting
steps.stepSummary: רבא says משה learned easy topics standing and difficult topics sitting.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Easy things he learned standing, and hard things he learned sitting.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a fourth answer. He splits the learning by how hard the material was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רב, רבא says each פסוק describes a different part of the learning. But רבא divides it by difficulty, not by learning versus reviewing. Hard material needs a calm, settled mind, so משה learned it sitting.

keyTerms.meaning: Easy (literally 'soft') material
Difficult (literally 'hard') material
In a standing position / in a sitting position

steps.whatToRemember: There are four answers to 'ואשב' versus 'עמדתי'. רב: stand to learn, sit to review. רבי חנינא: he was bowing. רבי יוחנן: 'ישיבה' means staying. רבא: easy material standing, hard material sitting.

phrases.english: Rava said: easy material while standing,
and difficult material while sitting.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: רַכּוֹת מְעוּמָּד וְקָשׁוֹת מְיוּשָּׁב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The fourth and final answer to the contradiction. It closes this side discussion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Split by how difficult the material was.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both verses describe the same learning in one posture.
steps.terutzMaskana: Easy material was learned standing and hard material sitting.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: one or two people reading the מגילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: whether one person reads the מגילה or two read it together, everyone has fulfilled the obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: If one person read it, or two people read it, they have fulfilled their obligation, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The side discussion about standing and sitting is over. The גמרא now quotes the next line of the משנה to set up a new discussion about two people reading the מגילה at the same time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line is a quote from the משנה, not a new teaching. It shows that two voices reading together still count for the listeners. The discussion that follows will explain why this works here even though it may not work in other places.

keyTerms.meaning: One person read it
Two people read it (together)
They fulfilled their obligation

steps.whyThisMatters: It opens a new topic: can people hear and fulfill a מצוה when two voices read at once?

phrases.english: If one read it, or two read it,
they have fulfilled their obligation, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the standing-and-sitting discussion and returns to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whether one person or two people read the מגילה, the listeners fulfill their obligation.
